title: JPMorgan says vendor cyberattack may have exposed customer names and email addresses; Visa and Mastercard cite third-party incidents
date_note: Date of JPMorgan's statement on X (Thursday 19 November), per Local 12/TNND and Reuters. The extortion group n0n claimed the data on 16 November, per Reuters.
geo_basis: bank's home market (United States) shown at New York; sources do not state a city
summary: JPMorgan says third-party vendors were the target of a cyberattack and it believes attackers accessed marketing data that may include some customer names and email addresses. Visa cites a third-party provider in Asia Pacific; Mastercard cites a third-party provider. Reuters says the extortion group n0n claimed data on 16 November; Reuters could not verify it. JPMorgan says there is no connection to an earlier-week service disruption.
plain: JPMorgan says outside vendors were attacked and some customers' names and email addresses may have been exposed. Visa and Mastercard also point to incidents at third-party providers.
exec: Vendor breaches reached marketing data at JPMorgan and were also cited by Visa and Mastercard, with a group claiming the data.
action: If you are a JPMorgan customer, expect direct contact from the bank and be wary of unexpected emails that use your name.
impact: JPMorgan: certain marketing data held by vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. Reuters review: more than 16,000 customer email addresses in the leaked material, unverified.

sources.name: The National News Desk via Local 12

validation.note: Reuters (via Business Insurance) and TNND (Local 12) each quote JPMorgan's statement on X. The n0n claim and its figures rest on Reuters alone and are unverified; Cybernews (403) and a note.com blog could not be used as sources.
